newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Tanker, bulk carrier collide off Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: Tanker, bulk carrier collide off Malaysia.

text.p: A tanker and bulk carrier collided at the weekend in the Strait of Malacca off Malaysia, creating a minor oil spill, a Maritime Rescue and Coordination Centre (MRCC) spokesman said on Tuesday.
The Cyprus-registered tanker "Saraband" and the bulk carrier "New Success" were both headed to Singapore, the spokesman said.
"There was an oil spill because the tanker's holding (tank) was slightly ruptured," the MRCC spokesman told Reuters by telephone from Port Klang near Kuala Lumpur.
"But the spill was minor and was taken care of by Malaysian authorities," he said.
The collision occurred at about 9.30 p.m. (1330 GMT) on Sunday, about eight miles off the southwestern port of Malacca in Malaysia.
Around 150 tonnes of bunker fuel spilled out of the Saraband, said the spokesman.
He said the vessels were travelling empty to Singapore to load cargo.
There were no casualties and both ships had been allowed to resume their journey after repairs, he said.
